chunks: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Glorious:
He عليه السلام said: "Part of that is combing the hair at every salat (prayer)."

key_terms.زِينَتَكُمْ: your adornment or beautification in preparation for worship
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship before which grooming is encouraged
key_terms.مَسْجِدٍ: place of prostration or worship, here in the Qur'anic phrase

ai.seo_question: What does "Take your adornment at every masjid" mean in relation to prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic command to take one's adornment at every masjid as including personal grooming before salat (prayer). It highlights cleanliness and presentability as part of proper devotional etiquette in worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.318 - Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) was asked about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious:
'Take your adornment at every place of worship.' (Surah Al-A’raf 7:31).
Imam (as) said: "Part of that includes combing one's hair before every prayer”.
